preamble: Clues supply tips associated with 5 down 23 across

clue.text: Adhering to socialist principles following Tories' first victory in part of contest

indicators.note: in places the pieces before it inside the part of contest

parts.note: a leg is one stage of a contest, as in a relay or a series of matches
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

indicators.note: first takes only the opening letter of Tories'

parts.note: a win is a victory

explanation.surface: After the Conservatives win one round, their opponents cling to socialist ideals.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the political left means holding socialist or progressive views.

clue.text: Murderous guy: 'How does it end?'

indicators.note: the question asks for the word's possible ending letters, and the reply joins them with or
end points to the letters at each end of guy

explanation.surface: A killer wonders aloud how his story will finish.
explanation.walkthrough: Ask how 'guy' ends and the answer is either end: G OR Y, which runs together as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gory means bloody and violent, the quality of a murderous scene.

clue.text: College's official notice lecturer's got in working party

indicators.note: got in means taken inside, so the notice and lecturer go within the working party

parts.note: a bee is a gathering for shared work, as in a sewing bee
an ad is a notice or advertisement
L is the abbreviation for lecturer; the 's stands for has

explanation.surface: A college notice says a lecturer has joined a working group.
explanation.definitionFit: A beadle is a ceremonial officer at some universities and colleges, leading processions.

clue.text: Old craft displayed by great striker keeping City up

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top
keeping means holding inside, so the great striker contains the city

parts.note: Brian Lara is a great West Indian batsman, a striker of the ball
York is an English cathedral city

explanation.surface: An old vessel shown off by a star footballer who keeps his club up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striker' points to football, but this is cricket's Brian Lara, a West Indian batting great; 'keeping' and 'up' do the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Ark Royal was the name of several Royal Navy ships, notably aircraft carriers, now retired.

clue.text: Upcoming event in which tri-champ and rider explode into action?

indicators.note: going into action means springing into motion, so these letters are shaken up

explanation.surface: A race where a jockey seeking a third win and his horse burst into action.
explanation.walkthrough: When the puzzle ran, Frankie Dettori and Enable were going for a third straight win in this race, hence 'tri-champ and rider'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arc is a top French horse race held each October, so the puzzle's week saw it coming up.

clue.text: Perpetual happiness finally found by not a large charwoman?

indicators.note: found by means placed beside, so what follows is set next to that letter
finally takes the last letter of happiness
not says the following letters are removed

parts.note: a tea lady serves tea in offices, broadly a charwoman's role

explanation.surface: A cleaner who is not large finds lasting happiness at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes A and L from TEALADY to leave TEADY.
explanation.definitionFit: Steady means constant and unchanging, close to unending or continuous.

clue.text: Feel unhappy about poetry putting oneself down?

indicators.note: about means going round, so the jumbled letters of feel surround the poetry
unhappy letters are disturbed, signalling that feel is rearranged

parts.note: odes are poems, so poetry gives ODES

explanation.surface: Someone feels low about their verse and keeps belittling themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unhappy' scrambles the first word before 'about' wraps it round the poems; the question mark flags the euphemism for suicide.
explanation.definitionFit: Felo de se is the old legal term for suicide, literally killing oneself, which a question mark lets 'putting oneself down' suggest.

clue.text: Learning is necessary, helping to raise the standard

indicators.note: to raise in a down clue means the letters are read upwards
helping means a portion, so the letters are a part of learning is necessary

explanation.surface: Education is essential, assisting efforts to lift standards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'helping' takes a portion of the words and 'to raise' reads it upwards: NGISNE becomes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensign is a flag, and a standard is likewise a flag carried as an emblem.

clue.text: In the light, dealer's ultimate object of quest!

indicators.note: In tells us the following pieces sit inside the light

parts.note: a ray is a beam of light

indicators.note: ultimate means last, so the final letter of dealer's is taken

parts.note: it is the pronoun standing for an object or thing

explanation.surface: A dealer is seen in good light, his last item being the one collectors hunt for.
explanation.walkthrough: R (dealer's last letter) and IT go 'In' RAY: RA-RIT-Y. Chambers and Collins both allow quest as a noun meaning the thing searched for.
explanation.definitionFit: A quest can be the object of a search, and a rare collectable is exactly what hunters seek.

clue.text: Not leave time to visit state

indicators.note: a visitor goes into a place, so time goes inside the word for state

parts.note: to state is to say

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to depart, saying it is time to visit a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: To remain where you are is the opposite of departing, so staying means not leaving.

clue.text: Deficits in coordination dip, as X-rays sadly show

indicators.note: sadly suggests things gone wrong, telling us the letters of dip, as X-rays are disordered

explanation.surface: A medical report: the X-rays show a regrettable dip in a patient's coordination.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyspraxia is a developmental condition affecting movement and coordination, so the plural names such impairments.

clue.text: Roget's last edition, which forms the basis of culture

definitions.text: which forms the basis of culture

indicators.note: last picks only the final letter of Roget's

parts.note: an issue is one edition of a publication

explanation.surface: The newest edition of Roget's Thesaurus is held up as a cornerstone of literary culture.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'culture' sound literary; here it is the laboratory sense, cells grown in a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Tissue culture grows living cells in a lab, so a sample of living cells is the material such a culture starts from.

clue.text: Eyed banking special credit to support class printing

indicators.note: banking means flanking on both sides, so eyed goes around the other pieces

parts.note: eyed means looked at, seen

indicators.note: to support in a down clue means sitting below, so special and credit come under class

parts.note: ilk means kind or class
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: A banker eyes special credit backing class-based printing.
explanation.definitionFit: Silkscreen is a stencil printing technique pushing ink through fine mesh, a form of printing.

clue.text: A radical unknown line taken by new clergy

indicators.note: taken by says the following letters are attached after the rearranged clergy
new means remade, so the letters of clergy are arranged afresh

parts.note: Y is a mathematical unknown, like x and z

explanation.surface: A political extremist with no known background joins the reformed clergy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A radical' sounds political, but in chemistry a radical is a group of atoms acting as a unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Glyceryl is the chemical group derived from glycerol, a radical in the chemist's sense of a bonded atom group.

clue.text: Chief supplier of element strong ale naturally retains

indicators.note: retains means holds within, so the answer is found inside the words strong ale naturally

explanation.surface: Strong ale, naturally, keeps its place as the main source of some vital ingredient.
explanation.definitionFit: Galena is lead sulphide, the principal ore from which the metal lead is extracted.

clue.text: Inducing sleep at last, spin concentric circles?

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of spin
concentric means sharing a centre, so a ring shape sits exactly in the middle of the other circle

parts.note: the Arctic Circle; with O, a letter shaped like a circle, the clue has two circles

explanation.surface: Sleep finally comes from spinning concentric circles, like a hypnotist's wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circles' gives both ARCTIC (as in Arctic Circle) and the round letter O; 'concentric' puts O in the exact centre: ARC-O-TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcotic drugs dull the senses and bring on drowsiness, so the adjective means sleep-inducing.

clue.text: It whitens stretch of shore round front of lake

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the stretch of shore goes about the next piece

parts.note: a beach is a stretch of shore

indicators.note: front of takes the first letter of lake

explanation.surface: Something that whitens a sandy stretch around the head of a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleach is the chemical agent that removes colour, making fabrics and surfaces whiter.

clue.text: No kid who plays trick

indicators.note: plays suggests the letters are messing about, so no kid who is rearranged

explanation.surface: A grown-up who plays a prank is no child.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoodwink is to deceive or dupe someone, which is to trick them.

clue.text: Goes missing at draws

indicators.note: missing says the word at is taken out

parts.note: goes as a noun are tries or attempts

explanation.surface: A sports report: someone misses at the draws.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw someone in is to lure or attract them, as temptation does.

clue.text: Not wriggling clear of porters, even in a pickle or jam?

indicators.note: wriggling clear of says the word not escapes from the jumbled letters of porters, even, and the rest are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in a jam who cannot wriggle free of the porters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wriggling clear of' takes N, O, T out of PORTERSEVEN and rearranges what remains. 'in a pickle' looks like the anagram signal but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A preserve is any fruit or vegetable kept in sugar or vinegar, so both pickle and jam are examples.

clue.text: Regarding Harcourt and Sheeran, say, as clarinet and saxophone?

parts.note: re means regarding or about
Ed Harcourt is an English singer-songwriter
Ed Sheeran is an English pop singer

explanation.surface: A musician asks about two singers called Ed and the wind instruments they play.
explanation.definitionFit: Clarinet and saxophone produce sound through a vibrating reed, so both are reed-fitted instruments.

clue.text: Good indication of the appearance of spring nuts?

definitions.text: Good indication of the appearance of spring
definitions.meaning: the bird whose call is the traditional first sign of spring in Britain

explanation.surface: A spring forecaster asking whether a good sign of the season is the arrival of nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, hearing the first cuckoo of the year is a traditional sign that spring has arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: The migratory bird's call heralds spring, and the same word is slang for crazy.

clue.text: In college, something for acting Head of English Language

indicators.note: In says the following letter is placed inside the acting part

parts.note: a role is a part for an actor

indicators.note: Head of takes the first letter of English

explanation.surface: At college, a part in a play for the Head of English Language.
explanation.definitionFit: A creole is a language that grew from a mix of others and became a community's mother tongue.

clue.text: See 5
Debt compiler has for Listener's ace, one of fifty

indicators.note: Listener's signals what a listener would hear, so the debt phrase is taken by its sound

parts.note: the setter (compiler, I) admitting a debt says I owe
A is the abbreviation for ace on playing cards

explanation.surface: A crossword setter owes something to The Listener's top solver, one of fifty people.
explanation.walkthrough: The Listener is a famously hard British crossword, and setters often call themselves 'I'. Spoken, I OWE plus A gives the state's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Iowa is one of the fifty states that make up the USA.

clue.text: Deprived of wings aviator gets woman

indicators.note: wings are the two sides, so the aviator loses his outer letters

parts.note: an airman is an aviator

explanation.surface: A pilot grounded and stripped of his wings finds a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wings' looks like the pilot's badge but means the outermost letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Irma is a female given name, so it can stand for a woman.

clue.text: Republican enemy brought to order by independent

indicators.note: bringing letters to order arranges them differently, so enemy is rearranged

explanation.surface: A Republican's opponent is disciplined by an independent politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Republican' suggests the US party, but it means a citizen of the Republic of Yemen.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Republic of Yemen is a citizen of a republic, so a republican in a literal sense.

clue.text: Extremely tough work environment causing various ailments

indicators.note: various means of differing kinds, so the letters of ailments appear in a different order

explanation.surface: A brutal workplace that leaves its staff with all kinds of health problems.
explanation.definitionFit: Working in the salt mines is an idiom for gruelling, monotonous toil, from the real hardship of mining salt.
